summary: A tight, dice-driven worker placement game where the numbers you roll dictate which actions you can take and how strong they are, with a central tug-of-war track for the shrine and moon-viewing bonuses driving tense positioning. It rewards efficient engine-building across several resource tracks (wisdom, honor tiles, cards) rather than any single dominant strategy, and plays fast for its weight.
praised: Elegant dice-as-workers mechanism where die value and color both matter
High player interaction via the shared influence track despite being a euro
Fast playtime relative to its strategic depth
Beautiful production and Japanese-castle theme integration
Multiple viable paths to victory (cards, tiles, dice sets)
criticised: Dice luck can swing which actions are available on a given turn
Rulebook/iconography has a learning curve up front
Some feel the theme is pasted onto a fairly abstract euro engine
Solo mode is decent but noticeably weaker than multiplayer

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial on the shared track and action spaces

scoring.why: Points come from combining honor tiles, card sets, temple/shrine track position, and end-game bonuses, so the winner is usually whoever built the most efficient multi-track engine.
